businessType: B2B SaaS company selling a vertical workflow platform to mid-market field-services firms (HVAC, plumbing, electrical contractors). 62 employees. Sales-led motion with SDR/AE teams and a 90-day average sales cycle. Founded 2019.
stage: $4.0M ARR, 50% YoY ARR growth (from $2.67M). Gross margin 78%. Burn $5.4M/yr, $9M cash, ~20 months runway. Blended (all-cohorts) CAC payback 10 months; blended LTV approximately $120,000 per customer; blended LTV:CAC approximately 4.1:1.
ownerGoal: Raise a $25M Series B in the next 4-5 months at a strong multiple, using best-in-class unit economics as the headline of the deck, then triple sales headcount to accelerate to $12M ARR within 24 months.
ownerConstraints: Runway constraint: 20 months of cash; the planned sales-headcount tripling assumes Series B closes; without it, the hiring plan is not fundable.
Team constraint: VP Sales hired 9 months ago and reorganized the AE pods; founder is reluctant to second-guess the new GTM structure publicly before the raise.
Investor constraint: Two term sheets are expected to hinge on the unit-economics story; founder has already socialized the 10-month payback / 4:1 LTV:CAC figures with prospective leads.
Data constraint: Finance team is 1.5 people; cohort-level reporting exists in the data warehouse but is not in the standard board deck, which shows blended metrics only.
Time constraint: Bankers want the deck finalized in 3 weeks; founder does not want to introduce analysis delay into the timeline.
immediateConcern: Founder framing: 'Our unit economics are a clear victory and the whole story of this raise. Blended CAC payback is 10 months and LTV:CAC is over 4:1 - top-decile for our stage. Growth is 50% and accelerating. I want to lead the Series B deck with unit economics, raise $25M, and pour it into tripling the sales team. The only real question is how fast we can hire AEs. I do not want to slow the raise down dissecting numbers that already look great.'
